title: Pasta with tomato-based sauce and beans or lentils

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with tomato-based sauce and beans or lentils is a dish of cooked pasta tossed in a sauce made from tomatoes, olive oil, garlic and herbs, combined with cooked beans (such as kidney beans, chickpeas) or lentils. The mix of carbohydrates, plant protein and fiber makes it a nutritious and filling meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that gives it a bright red color.
Legumes provide a high-quality plant protein and can help lower cholesterol levels.
The tradition of pairing pasta with beans dates back to Mediterranean cuisine, where such combinations have been prepared for centuries.
Lentils cook quickly and are a good source of iron, beneficial for blood health.
Legumes can enhance the absorption of minerals from tomatoes thanks to their vitamin C content.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Beans and whole‑grain pasta supply fiber that supports digestive health and regularity.

items.title: Plant‑based protein
items.content: The combination of pasta and beans/lentils provides all essential amino acids, useful for muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes in the sauce contain lycopene, which may reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and certain cancers.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Legumes slow carbohydrate absorption, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The dish delivers iron, magnesium, potassium and B‑vitamins.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, chickpeas or lentils.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Legumes contain phytates that can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or sprouting lessens this effect.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people; introduce them gradually.

items.title: Added salt in sauce
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, mixed with the tomato‑bean or tomato‑lentil sauce. Top with a drizzle of olive oil, fresh basil, grated Parmesan or a vegan cheese alternative. The dish stores well in the fridge and can be reheated in the microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked pasta in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions for up to 2 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving.
